evidence: Four P1 bypasses in scripts/lib/check-suite.js, all reproduced against main (7f7bddd) before building, all closed with a verdict re-derived PER CONSTRUCT rather than one applied to the class. (1) `#` MODELLED: an apostrophe inside a comment opened a real single-quote frame — shellOperators("npm run test:foo # don't forget this<NL>npm run bad ; npm run worse") returned [] while the apostrophe-free spelling returned [';','\\n']. Fail-closed was rejected because it fires on every ordinary script with a comment AND does not fix the defect. A comment begins ONLY at the start of a word, tracked FORWARD off the frame stack because a backwards byte test cannot separate `echo $(echo x)#y` (prints x#y) from `(echo a)#y` (prints a). (2) `<(`/`>(` MODELLED **AND** REPORTED — two decisions. The judge's proposal (a) as literally written (push a frame) would have left `npm run good <(npm run bad)` at []; mutation F2-b proves it. It is the worst SHELL_OPERATORS member: `bash -c 'true <(exit 7); echo exit=$?'` prints exit=0 — the inner status is discarded, not merged or last. Entering as well as reporting is measured, not assumed: 23 probes gave identical answers both ways and `cat <(echo a)#b ; npm run z` is the one that separates them (bash reports /dev/fd/63#b then runs SECOND). (3) Quoted YAML `run:` scalar MODELLED with a bounded escape table, residue FAIL-CLOSED as its own finding kind with its own remedy in check-ci-chains.mjs. (4) Plain multi-line continuation MODELLED — the only one reachable BY ACCIDENT (a contributor reflowing a long line), so a refusal would fire on a correct edit. IMPACT MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING: 0 of 114 governed commands (70 package.json scripts + 44 ci.yml run: values) contains `#`, `<(` or `>(`; 0 of 44 run: values is a quoted scalar or plain multi-line. No live verdict moves. ORACLE: checked against PyYAML 6.0.3 across 42 workflow shapes — 37 parse identically, 41 of 42 give the identical shell verdict; the one difference is a single-line block scalar whose trailing newline this parser trims, which is the better answer (a trailing newline is not a second command). ATTACKING MY OWN FIX found two false positives, both fixed here rather than left: `run: "npm run a" # note` is VALID YAML the first cut refused, and `run: | # note` is a block scalar whose indicator the regex missed and whose body the new fold then swallowed. FIFTEEN MUTATIONS; three survived and all three are resolved in the code: `!escaped.has(i)` was provably dead (escaped only holds indices the loop skips) and is deleted; two fold resets were mutually redundant — singly inert, jointly load-bearing — so one is deleted and the other now fails a test when removed; one guard is labelled tidiness rather than correctness because 45 inputs could not tell. TWO EXISTING ASSERTIONS pinning the OLD `#` over-report are rewritten, not deleted — the 'every unmodelled construct over-reports' claim was FALSE for `#`, over-reporting on the shape the test chose and under-reporting to nothing on the shape a person writes. RESIDUALS, ALL STATED: block scalars still trim their trailing newline and `run: >` still joins literally (both pre-existing, both pinned, neither changes a verdict); a comment that swallows the `)` of an unterminated substitution returns [] and bash refuses that string outright; `aliasLinks` still splits on a raw `&&` and knows nothing of `#` or `<(`; `|2` block indentation indicators are not honoured. FLOOR: npm run check 43 of 43 passed, 0 failed, 91.3s, exit 0, sandbox armed (denominator derived from STEPS.length, not recalled); test:check-suite 56 pass 0 fail (was 52); check:ci-chains clean and its failing branch executed by hand. NOT AN INDEPENDENT PANEL: this is the builder's own verification, single model family. The two advisory P3s from the judge round are deliberately NOT in this PR and are listed as follow-ups.
